title: 9 Warriors (Budget Core)

sources.label: ENDGAME Rank Up ALL ★★★ Warrior Build For Dota Auto Chess

body:
# 9 Warriors (Budget Core)

This is a low-roll, high-consistency build: instead of chasing a rare late-game
unit, it triples up the six cheapest Warriors (Axe, Mars, and Tusk at 1-cost,
Centaur Warrunner, Juggernaut, and Tiny at 2-cost) and then backfills the
board with whichever pricier Warriors are available to unlock the class's
level-9 bonus. Because the core is all 1- and 2-cost units, the pool is deep
and cheap re-rolls find them fast — the tradeoff is that Warriors deal
relatively little damage themselves and win primarily by refusing to die.
The build's real power spike is reaching 9 distinct Warrior pieces: at that
threshold the whole team reflects 1.5x its current armor as pure damage on
every hit taken, on top of the flat +11 armor the 6-piece bonus already
grants. Once armor-stacking items are online, that reflect effectively
punishes anyone who keeps attacking into the board.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Axe | 1 | Orc, Warrior | Early filler, pushed to 3★ first (cheap pool) |
| Mars | 1 | God, Warrior | Early filler, pushed to 3★ first |
| Tusk | 1 | Beast, Warrior | Early filler, easiest to sacrifice if contested |
| Centaur Warrunner | 2 | Centaur, Warrior | Primary damage — Double Edge hits self and nearby enemies, scaling off max HP |
| Juggernaut | 2 | Orc, Warrior | Secondary damage — spin grants brief magic immunity, key vs. casters |
| Tiny | 2 | Elemental, Warrior | Tank/HP battery — permanently gains HP each time it dies and revives |

Once the 6 low-cost Warriors are 3-starred, fill the remaining board slots
with any higher-cost Warriors you find (Doom, Kunkka, Slardar, Pudge, Huskar,
Wraith King, Troll Warlord, Sven, Primal Beast) purely to hit 9 distinct
Warrior pieces — they don't need to be starred up, they just need to be on
board. If one of the extras happens to carry the Naga tag (e.g. Slardar),
even better: it's a free second sub-synergy on top of the Warrior payoff.

## Items

Early game, prioritize anything that stacks armor or survivability cheaply:
**Vanguard** and **Sliver** are fine placeholders, but the real early-game
prize is **Pavise** — its passive has a chance to permanently add +1 armor to
its holder every time that unit takes damage in combat, so two or three
Pavise stacked on your frontline snowballs into 20+ bonus armor by the
midgame, which then feeds directly into the 9-Warrior reflect damage.

From there, prioritize Tier 3 items almost exclusively: **Aegis of
Immortal** (its damage-based-on-max-HP passive turns Centaur Warrunner's
self-inflicted Double Edge into a real damage source, and the extra life is
huge insurance), **Pipe of Insight** (cuts the self-damage from Double Edge
and adds magic resist — the single best item on Centaur Warrunner),
**Mekansm**, **Crimson Guard**, and **Shivas Guard** for more raw
armor/tankiness. **Heavens Halberd** is a strong pickup specifically against
enemy Demons (disarms their key damage dealer for several seconds).

Only start rolling for Tier 4-5 once the board is full and 3-starring has
stalled: **Giants Ring** and **Guardian Greaves** are the best Tier 4s for
sustain, and **Radiance** is excellent against Mage-heavy boards (evasion
plus guaranteed chip damage). For Tier 5, **Assault Cuirass** is the
standout — armor plus an attack-speed aura that also feeds the reflect —
followed by **Mirror Shield** and **Ogre Hood** as reasonable, if less
impactful, alternatives.

## Talent Picks

At the level-2 courier talent, take **Greedy** (-1 gold cost on units you
already own) — it directly subsidizes rolling for the third copies of your
core six. At level 3, the choice is **Guardian** (-20% damage taken) over
**Frenzy** (+30% lifesteal): Warriors don't deal enough damage for lifesteal
to matter much, but flat damage reduction stacks with the armor plan and
keeps you alive long enough for the reflect to matter.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Hold level 5 while win-streaking and just let 1-star Warriors accumulate;
level up to 6 only once your board is genuinely full and you need the extra
slot. Bank interest until you find a rare-unit relic (**Weighted Dice** for
cheaper re-rolls, or **Lucid Star** for a chance at instant 2-star units —
turn off auto-fuse when running Lucid Star so you don't accidentally burn a
2-star into a 3-star prematurely) and save it rather than popping it
immediately; activating it around round 15 gives you a long window (up to
round 25) to capitalize on it.

From round 15 onward, roll aggressively for the last copies of your Tier 1
and Tier 2 Warriors specifically — Juggernaut and Centaur Warrunner are the
priority 3-stars since they carry the actual damage, followed by Axe/Mars,
with Tiny and Tusk as the units you can most afford to leave behind. Stop
rolling the moment your board is full; overflowing the board risks
auto-selling a unit you need. By round 30 you should be at or pushing level
9 for the full Warrior bonus — falling behind that benchmark is the build's
biggest risk, since a half-finished 6-Warrior board doesn't hit nearly as
hard as a completed 9-piece one.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Warriors are all melee frontline units with no real backline carry, so
positioning is mostly about spreading them to soak as many opposing attacks
as possible rather than protecting a squishy — put Tiny (who wants to die
and revive with bonus HP) toward the front, and cluster Centaur Warrunner
and Juggernaut where their AoE/self-damage abilities land on the most
targets.

This build beats slower boards that rely on sustained physical or magical
DPS, since the reflect punishes exactly that. It struggles against: heavy
Mage boards (9 Mages or a Dragon/Mage burst combo can kill Warriors before
armor stacking or revives come online), Demon/Demon Hunter boards (true
damage and burn ignore armor), and Elf boards running illusions (illusions
copy your Warriors and can shred them since the copies don't respect the
reflect math the same way). Pure/true damage sources in general are the
build's kryptonite, and a well-itemized 2-3★ Chaos Knight can burst through
even a heavily armored frontline. Avoid contesting the build against another
player already committed to Warriors — splitting a shallow pool between two
players starves both of 3-stars.
